solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Panelling succeeds around a small bed

indicators.note: around says one word is wrapped about the next one, enclosing it

parts.note: to succeed is to win; third person
taken as written
a cot is a small bed, for a baby

explanation.surface: Someone describes a room where panelling has been fitted around a little bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Wainscot is wooden panelling lining the lower part of an interior wall.

clue.text: North London area's superior style

parts.note: arch means chief or superior, as in archbishop or arch-rival
a style or manner of doing something is a way

explanation.surface: A boast that one part of north London has a classier style than others.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the place to its wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Archway is a district of the borough of Islington in north London, named after its road bridge.

clue.text: Chamber group with a man lacking still?

parts.note: a nonet is a group of nine chamber musicians
he is the pronoun for a man
less means without or lacking, as in 'a year less a day'

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about whether a chamber ensemble is short of one player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like part of the question about the group, but it is the adverb meaning 'even so'.
explanation.definitionFit: Still and nonetheless both mean 'even so' or 'in spite of that', introducing a contrast.

clue.text: Rebuke clubs requiring mask

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
to mask something is to hide it

explanation.surface: A golf or card club is told off and made to wear a mask.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebuke someone is to scold or reprimand them, which is what chiding means.

clue.text: Deposed empress volunteers to ingest poison

indicators.note: to ingest is to take something inside the body, so one part swallows the other

parts.note: the TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
sarin is a deadly nerve agent

explanation.surface: A thriller plot in which a toppled empress has volunteers swallow poison.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army is Britain's part-time volunteer reserve, a staple crossword source for TA.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsarina was the wife of a Russian tsar or an empress in her own right; the last was deposed in 1917.

clue.text: Depend on artist? Hardly

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the usual crossword artist
to depend on is to rely on

explanation.surface: Asking whether one should trust an artist, and answering 'hardly'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depend on' looks like a single phrase, but 'on' is the placing word: the verb is put on, after, the artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardly and rarely both mean seldom or almost never, as in 'he hardly visits'.

clue.text: Algerian music numbers — southern Sahara lacks such

parts.note: rai is a style of Algerian popular music
nines are numbers
S is the abbreviation for southern

explanation.surface: A note on Algerian music and its numbers, sliding into the desert's dryness.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: the Sahara is a desert, so wet weather is what it lacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Raininess is the quality of being wet with rain, which a desert such as the Sahara notably lacks.

clue.text: Republican brought up to corruption

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Republican

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing something up means it reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A politician raised to a life of graft.
explanation.definitionFit: Rot means decay, and figuratively moral decay or corruption, as in 'the rot set in'.

clue.text: See first of keels in pound going up or down on canal

definitions.text: going up or down on canal

parts.note: lo is an old word for 'look' or 'see'

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: a pound is an enclosure for animals, like a cage

indicators.note: first of asks for only the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: the opening letter of keels

explanation.surface: Boating talk about watching keels in a pound, the stretch of canal between locks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' in the surface is the canal stretch between locks, but here it means an enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Lockage is the rise and fall of water levels, or of boats, in passing through a canal's locks.

clue.text: It bans a clinic under reconstruction taking in people?

indicators.note: something under reconstruction is being rebuilt in a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clinic being rebuilt bans admitting patients, as if it were a hospital refusing intake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking in people' looks like admitting patients, but the question mark flags eating them.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannibals eat human flesh, so a cannibalistic creature takes people in as food.

clue.text: Shroud the woman found outside temple

indicators.note: found outside says one word sits around the other, enclosing it

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a woman
a wat is a Buddhist temple in Thailand or Cambodia

explanation.surface: A woman found outside a temple wears a shroud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shroud' looks like a noun for burial cloth; here it is the verb to wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: To swathe is to wrap or envelop in cloth, as a shroud wraps a body; both are verbs here.

clue.text: Nearly miss one car reversing, tending to obstruct

indicators.note: reversing means going backwards, so the whole sequence reads from the end
nearly means not quite all, so the final letter of the next word is cut

parts.note: to miss something is to lack it
Roman numeral one
the Mini is a small British car

explanation.surface: A driver nearly clips another car while reversing and blocks the road.
explanation.walkthrough: LACK loses its last letter to LAC, then LAC, I and MINI read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Inimical means hostile or harmful, working against something, which is to tend to obstruct it.

clue.text: Hypocrisy accepted by one country for a spell

parts.note: Roman numeral one

indicators.note: something accepted by another is taken into it, so it goes inside

parts.note: a nation is a country
cant is hypocritical, pious talk

explanation.surface: A cynic remarks that one country tolerates hypocrisy for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spell' looks like a period of time, but it is a magic charm.
explanation.definitionFit: An incantation is a set of words chanted as a magic charm, which is a spell.

clue.text: Those actively promoting speed route for fast jumping?

parts.note: hypers are people who hype, promoting things vigorously
pace is speed

explanation.surface: Promoters urge speed along a route meant for quick jumps.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on science fiction, where ships 'jump' faster than light.
explanation.definitionFit: In science fiction, hyperspace is an extra dimension starships pass through to jump vast distances quickly.

clue.text: Second-year student hopes room is free

indicators.note: letters set free are loosed from their order and can be rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A student entering the second year hopes a room will be vacant.
explanation.definitionFit: In American schools and colleges a sophomore is a student in the second year.

clue.text: Hack chasing lead on cricket champ

indicators.note: chasing means following behind, so one piece comes after the other
the lead on a word is its front, so only the opening letter is wanted

parts.note: the opening letter of cricket
to hack at wood is to hew it

explanation.surface: A journalist pursues a story about a cricket champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champ' looks like a winner, but it is the verb meaning to munch noisily.
explanation.definitionFit: To champ is to munch or bite noisily, as a horse champs at the bit, which is to chew.

clue.text: A parliamentary session ends initially in recess

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially points to the starting letters of the words just before

parts.note: the opening letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A sitting of parliament closes as the house goes into recess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recess' looks like a parliamentary break; here it is an architectural alcove.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a semicircular recess, usually at the east end of a church.

clue.text: Help with homework handed over in advance

parts.note: prep is school homework, especially at British boarding schools
aid is help

explanation.surface: Assistance with homework given out before it is due.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handed over' looks like a reversal signal, but it belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prepaid has been paid, or handed over, before the goods or service arrive.

clue.text: Friendly greeting from rural workers around Lima

indicators.note: around says the first piece wraps about the next one

parts.note: the peasantry are farm labourers as a class
Lima is L in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Farmhands in Peru greet a visitor warmly.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes inside PEASANTRY after its P. Lima looks like Peru's capital; it is the code word for L.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasantry is a polite, friendly remark, such as a greeting exchanged in passing.

clue.text: Equestrian sport is short of time when the light goes

indicators.note: being short of something means lacking it, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: eventing is the horse-riding contest combining dressage, cross-country and jumping
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A horse show is running late and loses daylight.
explanation.walkthrough: EVENTING drops its T.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening is the part of the day at dusk, when daylight fades.

clue.text: Misrepresent volume editor over a text from antiquity

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece over another sits above it, coming first

parts.note: to rig results is to falsify or misrepresent them
V is the abbreviation for volume
ED is the abbreviation for editor
taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning against distorting an edited volume of an ancient text.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rig-Veda is the oldest of the Hindu Vedas, a collection of Sanskrit hymns over 3,000 years old.

clue.text: What could be part of a spray with stem gone bad

definitions.text: What could be part of a spray

indicators.note: gone bad suggests something spoiled, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A spray of flowers is spoiled because a stem has wilted.
explanation.walkthrough: A spray here is a brooch or jewelled ornament shaped like a sprig, not a flower bunch.
explanation.definitionFit: A jewelled spray is an ornament set with precious stones, so a gemstone can be part of one.

clue.text: Introduction to Fritz Lang and Mabuse's last projection

indicators.note: an introduction is the start, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of Fritz
taken as written

indicators.note: last points to the closing letter of the word before it

parts.note: the closing letter of Mabuse

explanation.surface: Introducing Fritz Lang's Dr Mabuse films and their last screening.
explanation.walkthrough: Fritz Lang directed the Dr Mabuse films, so 'projection' looks like a film showing; it is a protruding rim.
explanation.definitionFit: A flange is a projecting rim or collar on a pipe or wheel, used for strength or attachment.

clue.text: Bomb around large weapon

indicators.note: around says the first piece wraps about the next

parts.note: to bomb is to flop or fail
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A large explosive device described as a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A flail is a medieval weapon: a spiked ball or bar swung on a chain from a handle.

clue.text: Reliable writer, I have written about French cinematographer

parts.note: an author is a writer

indicators.note: written about means set down around something, so one part encloses another

parts.note: I've is the contraction of I have
Jacques Tati was a French film-maker, creator of Monsieur Hulot

explanation.surface: A dependable writer recalls composing a piece on a French film-maker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Written about' looks like the subject of the writing; it signals one piece wrapped round another.
explanation.definitionFit: Authoritative means trustworthy and accurate because it comes from an expert source, hence reliable.

clue.text: Nectar-seeking flier from group of Noctuidae

indicators.note: from a group of letters means the result is taken out of a run within the next word

parts.note: found inside this word

explanation.surface: A nectar-feeding insect from the Noctuidae, a family of moths.
explanation.walkthrough: The Noctuidae are owlet moths, which do feed on nectar, so the surface wants an insect; the answer is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The tui is a New Zealand honeyeater bird that feeds largely on flower nectar.

clue.text: Warning a tool is wasting energy

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: wasting something means losing it, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: a device is a tool or gadget
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A caution that some gadget squanders power.
explanation.walkthrough: DEVICE drops its first E.
explanation.definitionFit: Advice can mean a warning or notice given to guide someone's conduct, as in advice against travel.

clue.text: Type of apple no good, nearly all Asian rootstock for cooking

indicators.note: nearly means not quite complete, so the final letter is cut off

parts.note: Gala is an apple variety
NG is the abbreviation for no good
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook rejects one kind of apple and almost all Asian roots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rootstock' looks like orchard grafting, fitting the apple; here it is a rhizome.
explanation.definitionFit: Galangal is the aromatic rhizome of a ginger-family plant used in South-East Asian cooking.
